name: Bedaquiline
route_note: Oral tablets with food, typically a loading phase followed by thrice-weekly or daily dosing within combination regimens.

discovery.note: Identified by whole-cell screening against Mycobacterium smegmatis; reported in Science in 2005.

tagline: First new-mechanism TB drug in decades, backbone of all-oral drug-resistant TB regimens
summary: Bedaquiline is a diarylquinoline that inhibits mycobacterial ATP synthase. Approved in 2012 as the first new tuberculosis drug with a novel mechanism in about 40 years, it is now the backbone of WHO-recommended all-oral regimens such as BPaLM for rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis.
mechanism: Bedaquiline binds the c-subunit ring (and the a-subunit interface) of mycobacterial F1Fo-ATP synthase, stalling rotation and blocking ATP production. It kills both replicating and dormant M. tuberculosis, with a delayed bactericidal effect, and is highly selective over the human mitochondrial enzyme.

Resistance occurs through atpE target mutations or, more commonly, through mutations in Rv0678 that upregulate the MmpS5-MmpL5 efflux pump, which also reduces susceptibility to clofazimine. Its very long terminal half-life reflects slow release from tissues.
uses: Pulmonary multidrug-resistant and rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis, as part of combination therapy (adults and children)

history.title: Discovery published
history.detail: Andries and colleagues describe TMC207 in Science.

history.title: US accelerated approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Sirturo for MDR-TB with a boxed warning about increased mortality and QT prolongation in a phase II trial.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: Sirturo receives a conditional marketing authorisation in the EU.

history.title: BPaL regimen
history.detail: Bedaquiline is approved for use with pretomanid and linezolid for highly drug-resistant TB (Nix-TB).

history.title: WHO BPaLM
history.detail: WHO recommends six-month BPaLM (bedaquiline, pretomanid, linezolid, moxifloxacin) for rifampicin-resistant TB.

history.title: Patent challenge
history.detail: India's patent office rejects a secondary patent on bedaquiline; Johnson & Johnson later says it will not enforce secondary patents in many low- and middle-income countries.

serious: Increased mortality observed in the original phase II trial
safety.boxed_warning: The original US label carried a boxed warning for increased mortality and QT prolongation, based on the C208 phase II trial.

facts: Bedaquiline was the first FDA-approved drug specifically for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis.
Strong CYP3A4 inducers such as rifampicin markedly lower bedaquiline exposure and are avoided with it.
